faqs.question: What is the 100e used for?
faqs.answer: The 100e is a streamlined, single-channel 100 MHz benchtop NMR spectrometer used for high-resolution 1H and/or 19F acquisition. It's built for labs that need the sharpest possible single-nuclei data using standard 5mm tubes.

faqs.question: Why does the 100e only support single-channel acquisition?
faqs.answer: The 100e is designed as a single-channel instrument specifically to deliver the highest resolution in the Nanalysis series for 1H and/or 19F work. Focusing on a single channel removes the tradeoffs that come with multinuclear flexibility.

faqs.question: What engine powers the 100e?
faqs.answer: The 100e runs on the RS2D CAMELEON4 engine, the same high-performance platform behind Nanalysis's market-leading 100 MHz field strength and resolution.

faqs.question: How does Wiley KnowItAll work with the 100e?
faqs.answer: Wiley KnowItAll pairs directly with the 100e for rapid, reliable chemical fingerprinting. It allows precise compound identification without requiring a dedicated NMR spectroscopy expert on staff.

faqs.question: What tube size does the 100e use?
faqs.answer: The 100e uses standard 5mm NMR tubes, so it fits into existing lab consumable workflows without special equipment.

faqs.question: Can I customize pulse sequences on the 100e?
faqs.answer: Yes, the 100e supports pulsed field gradient-based pulse programs, and sequences can be modified or programmed without needing to learn a pulse programming language.

faqs.question: How is the 100e different from the 100Pro?
faqs.answer: The 100e is a single-channel, single-nuclei instrument built for the highest possible 1H/19F resolution, while the 100Pro is a multinuclear system for labs needing broader nuclei coverage. Inkarp can help confirm which fits your specific workflow.

faqs.question: Which industries use the 100e?
faqs.answer: The 100e is used across pharmaceuticals and biotechnology, polymer and materials research, synthetic chemistry, reaction monitoring, and academic teaching, wherever high-resolution single-nuclei data is the priority.

sections.title: Single Nuclei Focus and Resolution
sections.tabSummary: Why streamlined beats multinuclear for 1H/19F work
body: This section covers why the 100e's single-channel design delivers the series' highest resolution.
Choosing single-nuclei focus over multinuclear flexibility is a genuine tradeoff, and the 100e is built for labs where that tradeoff makes sense.

By concentrating entirely on 1H and/or 19F acquisition, the 100e reaches the highest resolution available anywhere in the Nanalysis series. That focus matters most for labs running consistent 1H or 19F workflows, like reaction monitoring, structure confirmation, or quantitative polymer analysis, where the extra channels of a multinuclear system add cost without adding value. The same RS2D CAMELEON4 engine that powers Nanalysis's broader 100 MHz platform sits underneath the 100e, so the resolution gain doesn't come at the cost of the platform's core performance.

groups.note: Tell our team your primary nucleus of interest, and Inkarp will confirm whether the 100e's single-channel focus fits or whether a multinuclear system makes more sense.

faqs.question: How do I control flow experiments on the Nanalysis-60?
faqs.answer: Flow experiments can be initiated directly on the instrument, through NMReady-CONNECT, or through third-party software, depending on how your lab is set up.

faqs.question: Is the Nanalysis-60 cryogen-free?

sections.title: Automated Sampling with AUTOsample-60
body: This section covers how the AUTOsample-60 accessory automates sample queueing on the Nanalysis-60.
Running samples one at a time works fine for occasional use, but most labs eventually need more throughput than that allows. The AUTOsample-60 is built for that shift.

It mounts on top of the Nanalysis-60 and switches quickly between autosampler and manual modes, without requiring any extra bench space. Two carousels, each holding 25 tubes, give it a 50-tube capacity. Onboard queueing software handles the rest: assign an experiment to each tube, and the system runs through them automatically, without needing someone at the bench for every sample.

rows: Onboard queueing software assigns experiments per tube
Flexibility between automated and manual use

groups.note: Tell our team your typical daily sample volume, and Inkarp will confirm whether the AUTOsample-60 fits your throughput needs.

groups.title: Real-Time Reaction Monitoring with the Flow Kit
groups.summary: Turning the instrument into an online detector
groups.description: This section covers how the Flow Kit turns the Nanalysis-60 into an online NMR detector.
body: Some workflows need to see a reaction as it happens, not just analyze a sample after the fact. The Flow Kit is what makes that possible on the Nanalysis-60.

It converts the instrument into an online NMR detector, usable on its own or alongside other analytical techniques already in your lab. That opens up real-time reaction understanding and optimization, automated repeated syntheses, and tighter integration into a broader laboratory system. The NMR flow-through cell itself is easy to install and can be sealed from the environment, and experiments can be started directly on the instrument, through NMReady-CONNECT, or through third-party software depending on how your lab is set up.

faqs.question: What is the 60e used for?
faqs.answer: The 60e is a compact, single-channel 60 MHz benchtop NMR spectrometer used for routine screening of 1H and 19F spectra. It's built for teaching labs, QA/QC screening, and general structural verification.

faqs.question: How does One Touch automation work on the 60e?
faqs.answer: One Touch is the 60e's automated analysis button, which launches a full acquisition without manual parameter setup. Data can be returned in as little as four seconds.

faqs.question: Why is the 60e single-channel?
faqs.answer: The 60e is designed as a single-channel instrument to keep routine 1H and 19F screening simple, fast, and affordable. Labs needing additional nuclei typically look at a multinuclear option like the 60Pro.

faqs.question: Does the 60e need regular maintenance?
faqs.answer: No, the 60e uses a permanent magnet with no cryogens, so it doesn't require weekly or preventive maintenance. Automatic testing and standby mode keep it ready for use.

faqs.question: Is the 60e suitable for teaching labs?
faqs.answer: Yes, the 60e is widely used in academic teaching labs because its simple interface and One Touch operation let students prepare, acquire, and process their own NMR spectra directly in class.

faqs.question: What tube size does the 60e use?
faqs.answer: The 60e uses standard 5mm NMR tubes, so it fits into conventional sample preparation workflows without special consumables.

faqs.question: How is the 60e different from the 60Pro?
faqs.answer: The 60e is a single-channel instrument focused on 1H and 19F acquisition, while the 60Pro is a dual-channel, multinuclear spectrometer for broader analytical needs. Inkarp can help confirm which fits your workflow.

faqs.question: How much does the 60e weigh?
faqs.answer: The 60e is a lightweight instrument, making it easy to site or move within a lab or classroom.

faqs.question: What is the price of the 60e in India?
faqs.answer: The price of the 60e in India depends on your configuration and any accessories selected. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your requirements are confirmed.

body.text: The 60e is single-channel by design, focused on 1H and 19F acquisition, which keeps the instrument simple, affordable, and fast to run.
Its One Touch button launches a fully automated analysis, so results don't depend on manual setup or specialist NMR knowledge.
Data acquisition can happen in as little as four seconds, making routine screening genuinely quick rather than a scheduled task.
A permanent magnet with no cryogens means no weekly or preventive maintenance, and the instrument stays ready for use through automatic testing and standby mode.
Standard 5mm NMR tubes keep sample preparation conventional, with no special consumables required.
It's light enough and simple enough to be a genuine teaching tool, letting students prepare samples, set parameters, and acquire and process their own spectra directly in the lab.
The same simplicity that makes it approachable for students also makes it a dependable, affordable QA/QC tool for industrial analysis.
It plugs into a standard wall outlet and can be set to energy-saving mode when not in use, keeping running costs low.

sections.title: One Touch Automation and Ease of Use
sections.tabSummary: How routine screening becomes a one-button task
body: Routine screening shouldn't need a specialist standing by, and the 60e is built around that idea.

Pressing the One Touch button launches a fully automated analysis, taking the instrument through acquisition without manual parameter setup. Data can come back in as little as four seconds, which turns what used to be a scheduled task into something you can run between other work. The software interface stays simple and intuitive by design, reducing operational complexity so a new user can get reliable results quickly, and data can be saved, printed, exported, or processed using common third-party software.

groups.description: Learning NMR by watching a demonstration is one thing. Running your own sample and interpreting your own spectrum is another, and that's where the 60e earns its place in teaching labs.

Students can prepare samples, load and manipulate parameters, and personally acquire and process their own NMR spectra, developing the same experimental skills they'll carry into research work later.
